properties.snippet: Alcohol bans prohibit the drinking and possession of alcohol in some public places in Auckland, like parks and streets, at certain times.
properties.description:
The Alcohol Control Area dataset includes a register of current permanent and temporary alcohol bans in Auckland.

Alcohol bans prohibit the drinking and possession of alcohol in some public places in Auckland, like parks and streets, at certain times. Some bans are in place 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Other bans are in place only at night-time or during daylight savings.

The bans aim to reduce crime and disorder in public places.

properties.snippet: This polygon feature class contains all lands that are owned and/or maintained by Auckland Council Community Facilities (CF) Department, and in some cases by other Council-owned and controlled organisations, that are generally parks and open spaces.  These include Pocket Parks, Neighbourhood Parks, Suburb Parks, Destination Parks, Connection and Linkage Open Space, Civic Space, Conservation Open Space and Organised Sports Open Space.  Also included are cemeteries, and other reserve lands that are used for stormwater, esplanade reserves, etc.  The boundaries drawn in this dataset are NOT legal boundaries; rather these boundaries represent the areas or sites that Auckland Council maintains through its full facility contractors.  Also, this dataset DOES NOT represent the legal status of the land, i.e. whether the land is gazetted under the Reserve Act, subject under the Local Government Act or other statutory provisions. The polygons represent the maintenance extent on the land.
properties.description:
Purpose:

This data is primarily used by council and its contractors in managing and maintaining all parks, reserve and open spaces across Auckland region.

Lineage:

This data was a product of consolidating legacy GIS datasets from the previous regional council and seven city and district councils. Since amalgamation in 2010, the data has been updated by Asset Management teams. The extent of park boundaries were defined from the Core Record System (CRS) Parcel Boundaries supplied by Land Information New Zealand (LINZ).

Creation Date:

1/04/2012

Update Cycle:

Quarterly

properties.snippet: Land cover across the Auckland Region classified into impervious surface types.
properties.description:
Impervious surfaces—mainly artificial structures such as pavements, roads, sidewalks, driveways and parking lots, as well as industrial areas such as airports, ports and logistics and distribution centres that are covered by water-resistant materials such as asphalt, concrete, brick, stone—including rooftops, were mapped along with other surface types to produce the following categories:

• Buildings (Class Name = 0)

• Other impervious (driveways, carparks, etc) (Class Name = 2)

• Roads (Class Name = 3)

Image processing was conducted by Lynker Analytics using machine learning techniques on Auckland Council’s most recent orthophotography—7.5 cm pixel resolution (2017) covering all the region’s urban settlements and beyond; and 50 cm pixel resolution (2010-2012) covering the region’s remaining, predominantly rural areas—to produce two separate (urban and rural) land cover datasets.

Land Cover 2017 is the companion dataset to Impervious Surfaces.

A copy of the full background report can be obtained from the Regional Planning team in Auckland Council’s Healthy Waters department.
